newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-HIROSHIMA MISSES OUT AS 2002 WORLD CUP VENUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HIROSHIMA MISSES OUT AS 2002 WORLD CUP VENUE.

text.p: Japan's 2002 World Cup organisers on Wednesday named the 10 sites where its matches would be played in the joint hosting of the event with South Korea but surprisingly did not include the atomic bomb city of Hiroshima and the capital Tokyo.

The venues chosen include Yokohama, a port city south of Tokyo, which is a possible site for the final, Sapporo, capital of Japan's northernmost island of Hokkaido, and Oita on southern Kyushu island, the Japan Football Association said in an announcement.
The other venues are the port city of Kobe in central Japan, Osaka, Saitama, immediately north of Tokyo, Miyagi in northeastern Japan, Shizuoka, Niigata and Ibaraki.
"We have selected the venues after comprehensively studying various criterion in order to make the World Cup a success," association president Ken Naganuma told a news conference.
"It was a painful decision," he added.
The football association was forced to choose from among 15 candidate venues after FIFA, soccer's world governing body, decided last May to split the finals between the two countries.
South Korea has not announced its venues yet.
Joao Havelange, president of FIFA, soccer's world governing body, had personally pushed for Hiroshima as a venue because of its significance as the world's first city to have suffered an atomic bomb.
More than 140,000 people were killed in Hiroshima on August 6, 1945, nine days before Japan surrendered in World War Two.
But the city virtually ruled itself when local authorities refused to comply with a FIFA ruling which required two-thirds of the seating at World Cup stadiums be covered with a roof.
"We did our best. We deeply regret the result," Hiroshima mayor Takeshi Hiraoka said.
"We are not in a financial situation where we can spend a huge amount of money to build the roof," he added.
It would cost an estimated 15 billion yen ($131 million) to construct the necessary roof.
The venue for the final, to be played in Japan, was not announced but it is widely tipped to be Yokohama.
